name: Mikasa
description: You are given two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$. Find the $$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ of the sequence $$$n \oplus 0, n \oplus 1, \ldots, n \oplus m$$$. Here, $$$\oplus$$$ is the bitwise XOR operator . $$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ of the sequence of non-negative integers is the smallest non-negative integer that doesn't appear in this sequence. For example, $$$\operatorname{MEX}(0, 1, 2, 4) = 3$$$, and $$$\operatorname{MEX}(1, 2021) = 0$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 30\,000$$$)  — the number of test cases. The first and only line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$0 \le n, m \le 10^9$$$).
output_specification: For each test case, print a single integer  — the answer to the problem.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).
